tasks.title: Give the trench garrison counts a plate; they are unreadable
tasks.why: MEASURED, Captures/hud-1103/armed-he.png and base-1920.png with crop-cluster-full.png and crop-catchip.png. Every category chip in a trench order cluster paints its count straight onto the unit portrait behind it, with only the 1 px outline in BattleHud.uss:173 (-unity-text-outline-width: 1px, colour #0A0B0C). Measured as local Weber contrast per glyph pixel (the pixel against the median of a 9x9 ring around it), all six chips in armed-he.png read: RIFLE p10 0.34 median 0.98, ASSAULT 0.41/0.92, MG 0.64/1.27, OFFICER 0.58/1.06, SHIELD 0.69/1.58, ENGINEER 0.52/1.62, and between 30% and 57% of each glyph's pixels sit below contrast 1.0. The HUD's own standard for a number, measured the same way in the same frame, is the gauge digits on their tw-window plates: '52' p10 7.37 median 7.52 and '3793' p10 8.52 median 10.06. The counts are therefore 11x to 25x below the standard the rest of the HUD holds, and base-1920.png confirms it in a second frame ('14' p10 0.25, median 0.82, 54% of glyph pixels under 1.0). These six numbers are what a player reads before he sends a trench over the top - how many riflemen, how many guns, how many officers are actually in it - and the box they live in is 12x25 capture px at 1920 (20x25 for a wide number), about 6 px a digit, falling to roughly 8x17 at 1280x720. GUESS: a 1 px outline cannot carry a bold mono caption over painted art at this size; every other number on this HUD sits in a recessed tw-window.
tasks.done_when: A script crops every hud-cat-chip count out of a fresh HudCapture.Shoot at 1920x1080 and at 1280x720, using that capture's own sidecar rects, and asserts the local Weber contrast of its glyph pixels is p10 >= 3.0 with under 5% of glyph pixels below 1.0, while the same frame's gauge digits still measure above it. It fails today on all six chips at both sizes (worst p10 0.34, best 0.69).

tasks.title: Stop the speaker plate covering the trench order cluster's chips
tasks.why: MEASURED, Captures/hud-1103/base-1920.png with crop-rightband.png (x 1100-1920, y 670-840) and crop-orders.png. With a unit speaking, the dialogue plate is raised to .hud-dialogue--raised (BattleHud.uss:104: 'left: auto; right: 14px; bottom: 234px', commented 'no room beside the bar: over its right end'), which puts it at y 690-800 on the right of the screen - the same band a trench order cluster occupies. A pixel scan along y=700 finds the plate's dark outer rim at x 1490-1491 (10,11,12) and its flat plate colour (34,36,39) from x=1494, while that capture's own sidecar puts orders at [1139,708,408,113], ending at x=1547: 53 px of the cluster lie under the plate, and the frame shows the second category chip sliced vertically at x=1494 with everything right of it gone. BattleHud.uxml puts orders-layer first on purpose ('under every panel, so a trench's buttons never cover the selection or the bar'), so the cluster always loses this fight. The cost: a unit crying 'I'm done for... get the crew out!' is exactly the moment a player reaches for that trench, and the chips he must click to choose who goes over the top are hidden and unclickable under the plate reporting the emergency. It bites on any trench near the right of the screen, which is the direction the player pushes. The same frame also shows that the dialogue plate is not in HudCapture.Probes (nor are hover-card and aim-readout), which is why its edge had to be found by a pixel scan rather than read from the sidecar; adding it is what makes the fix checkable. This finding rests on one frame: a second capture with a speaker up and a trench cluster deliberately placed at the right edge would settle how often it bites.
tasks.done_when: 'dialogue' is added to HudCapture.Probes, and a PlayMode test raises a dialogue line while a trench order cluster is on screen at the right edge and asserts the dialogue element's worldBound does not intersect any visible .hud-cat-chip or .hud-orders__btn; plus a fresh HudCapture.Shoot in that state whose sidecar 'dialogue' and 'orders' rects do not overlap. It fails today with 53 px of overlap.
